clue.text: Baffled to be dismissed

blocks.note: first meaning: puzzled, at a loss
second meaning: out in cricket when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket with the batter out of the crease

explanation.surface: Someone confused at being sent away or fired.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket sense is the key: a batter is stumped when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while they are out of their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past participles: perplexed people are said to be stumped, and stumping is one way a cricket batter gets out.

clue.text: Ahead in series, not half great

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word series is kept, the rest discarded
in places the first piece inside the letters of the second

blocks.note: a team that is ahead is up
the first half of the word series

explanation.surface: A team leading a sporting series, not quite at its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half great' sounds like British slang for very great, but 'not half' trims series to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal adjective for excellent or wonderful, a common colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Disagreeable, being shattered as you've run short of energy

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter for energy is removed
something shattered is broken into pieces, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words, taken as written
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Feeling exhausted and grumpy after a run that drained your energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one E from AS YOU'VE RUN, then rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsavoury describes something unpleasant or objectionable, a close synonym for disagreeable.

clue.text: Expert with good idea receiving endless criticism over a forecast

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for criticism is cut off
receiving means the idea word takes the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: a pro is an expert or professional
G is the standard abbreviation for good
a notion is an idea
stick, slang for criticism, minus its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pundit with a bright idea takes flak over a prediction.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone stick is British slang for criticising them. In a down clue 'over' means above, so the trimmed criticism sits on top of A inside the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognostication is a prediction of future events, so it serves as a noun synonym for a forecast.

clue.text: Stranger getting into yard, climbing, not steady

indicators.note: getting into puts the first word inside the abbreviation for yard
in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: YD is the abbreviation for yard
odder means more strange

explanation.surface: An unfamiliar person wanders into a garden, clambering about unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for a person, but it is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery describes someone shaky or tottering, typically through age, so it means unsteady on one's feet.

clue.text: Be back in charge, giving discount

indicators.note: back means the word be is read from right to left
in puts the turned word inside the word for charge

blocks.note: taken as written
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A manager returning to run the shop and handing out reductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'charge' supplies a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is a partial refund or reduction in the amount owed, so it is a kind of discount.

clue.text: Arbiter with regard to quiet update

blocks.note: ref is short for referee, an arbiter
re means concerning or with regard to
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A referee asks for silence before announcing an update on a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh a page or data is to update it with the latest version, both verbs of renewing.

clue.text: Begin an absurdly chaotic charity event

indicators.note: chaotic means disordered, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Starting a fundraiser that turns out absurdly disorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: A bring-and-buy sale is a British fundraiser where people donate goods and buy others' donations. 'absurdly' looks like an anagram signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Such sales are typically held by churches and schools to raise money for good causes, so they are charity events.

clue.text: Greek character exercises in shade

blocks.note: tau is the Greek letter T
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A Greek person working out in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests shelter from the sun, but here it means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a brownish-grey colour, and a shade is a particular variety of colour.

clue.text: Unjustly, first off, going after saint forcefully

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter of the word for unjustly is removed

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
wrongly means unjustly; drop its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly and aggressively pursuing a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going after saint' places the trimmed word after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongly and forcefully are adverbs for acting with great power or vigour.

clue.text: Nothing after seconds covered with favourite sauce

indicators.note: covered with means the abbreviation for seconds sits inside the favourite word

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
S is the abbreviation for seconds
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Going back for second helpings of a favourite sauce and finding none left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts O at the end of the covered piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and cheese, eaten with pasta.

clue.text: Disagree without hesitation with one religious group, being tough

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is taken out of the word for disagree

blocks.note: differ means disagree; remove its last two letters
er is a sound of hesitation, the part removed
I is the Roman numeral one
a cult is a religious group

explanation.surface: Someone who dissents firmly from a sect, standing tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficult and tough are adjectives describing something hard to do or deal with.

clue.text: Regret restricting equal income

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the regret word holds the equal word

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
even means equal or level

explanation.surface: Lamenting a cap on equal pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, especially an organisation's or government's earnings, so it means income.

clue.text: English company led by composer, not a painter

indicators.note: not a means a letter A is dropped from the composer's name
led by means the following pieces come behind the composer, who goes in front

blocks.note: Elgar, the English composer, without an A
E is the abbreviation for English
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An English ensemble directed by a composer, though not by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led by composer' means the composer comes first. 'not a painter' sounds like a description but 'not a' trims the composer and 'painter' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born Spanish Renaissance artist famous for elongated religious figures, a painter.

clue.text: Creative technique from sad broadcaster with insubstantial piece

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
thin means flimsy, insubstantial
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A gloomy TV presenter offering a flimsy item on brainstorming methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is a chessman, not a portion or article.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-sky thinking is the business idea of brainstorming without practical limits, a method for generating original ideas.

clue.text: Poor batting, then time for banter

blocks.note: poor means bad
a batting side in cricket is in
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dismal innings with the bat, followed by some teasing chat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is said to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, witty conversation, the light teasing exchange that banter also names.

clue.text: Silly line on wine, cold and unyielding

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the next word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A foolish remark about chilled wine from someone stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the anagram before the wine in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic means not stretchy or flexible, so a thing that does not give is unyielding.

clue.text: Variety of hybrid barley got for an unfair price

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer obtained a new strain of crossbred grain at a rip-off cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' looks like a plant strain alongside the barley, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a charge so blatantly excessive that it amounts to open theft, an overcharge.

clue.text: Bag in room containing antique

indicators.note: containing means the room word holds the antique word inside

blocks.note: a hall is a room
antique means old

explanation.surface: A bag left in a room full of antiques.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travelling case, so it is a kind of bag.

clue.text: Inexperience shown by muddled answers

indicators.note: muddled means confused, so the letters of the next word are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A novice giving confused replies in an exam or interview.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawness is the state of being new and untrained, as with a raw recruit, so it means lack of experience.

clue.text: Final gathering for dancing and sport

blocks.note: a net figure is final, after all deductions
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: The last party of the season, with dancing and games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' looks like the end of a tournament, but it means net, as in a net price.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team ball game, popular in Britain and the Commonwealth, where goals are scored through a high hoop.

clue.text: Number worth re-examining to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so the answer is a portion of the words before

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A figure that merits a second look, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a cardinal number, the integer after two, so it is a specific example of a number.

clue.text: Style with attraction turning erratic

indicators.note: turning means the attraction word is turned round and read backwards

blocks.note: a way is a manner or style
a draw is an attraction, something that pulls crowds

explanation.surface: A fashion with appeal changing unpredictably.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayward describes behaviour that is unpredictable, wilful and hard to control, so it means erratic.

clue.text: Unknown quantity produced upset in horse race

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns
bred means produced offspring

explanation.surface: A surprise result at a famous race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suggests a shock win in racing, but it turns over the whole string of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is the famous flat race for three-year-olds run at Epsom, England, and the name is used for similar races.

clue.text: Develop garden's front end, having time off

indicators.note: front means only the first letter of the word garden's is kept
having time off means the abbreviation for time is removed from the word for end

blocks.note: the opening letter
to terminate is to end; drop T for time

explanation.surface: Plants growing at the far end of a garden while someone takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' looks like a noun after 'front', but it is the verb terminate, minus T.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is for a seed to begin growing and sprouting, so it means to develop.

clue.text: Table, aluminium object? Get away

indicators.note: get away is read as an instruction to send off the letters of get

blocks.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
a target is an object or aim; remove get

explanation.surface: Someone asks what an aluminium table is meant to be, and is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get away' sounds like a dismissal, but it tells you to remove GET from TARGET.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the raised table in a church at which communion is celebrated, so a table is a fair definition.

clue.text: Herb in north-east between marsh and lake

indicators.note: between means the compass letters sit in the gap separating the marsh and the lake

blocks.note: a fen is a marsh
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A wild plant growing in north-east England between a marsh and a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in north-east' reads as a location, but 'in' just joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fennel is an aniseed-flavoured plant whose leaves and seeds are used in cooking, a herb.

clue.text: Vague, not confident about conclusion of work and so on

indicators.note: conclusion of means only the last letter of the word work is taken
about means the word for not confident goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: shy means lacking confidence
the final letter
etc, et cetera, means and so on

explanation.surface: An unsure student, hazy about how to finish an essay and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy means lacking detail or thoroughness, as a rough sketch does, so it means imprecise or vague.
